issues.description: Interface name mismatch for the 'rideable' concept: the problem statement and UML declare an interface named 'Rideable' with an abstract method messageOnRide(), and the template Main uses Rideable (Rideable[]). The solution repository, however, defines an interface named 'Mountable' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Mountable.java) and has Pig.java and Seal.java implement Mountable. Meanwhile Rideable.java in the solution repository is present but empty. This inconsistent naming (Rideable vs Mountable) across problem statement/template and solution will confuse students and may cause compilation or grading mismatches because code expecting Rideable will not match the solution implementations that use Mountable.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name for the rideable concept across all artifacts. Preferred option: rename the solution's Mountable interface to Rideable (move/rename src/de/tum/cit/ase/Mountable.java -> src/de/tum/cit/ase/Rideable.java) and update Pig.java and Seal.java to implement Rideable. Ensure Rideable.java declares the method String messageOnRide(). Alternatively, if Mountable is the intended canonical name, update the problem statement, UML, and template code to refer to Mountable and populate/replace the empty Rideable.java in the solution. Ensure only one interface name is used so template tests, problem description, and solution code align.
